gallery.caption: Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly.
gallery.title: The four stages of a butterfly

objectives: Name the four stages a butterfly goes through.
Tell the difference between a caterpillar and a chrysalis.
Find a butterfly egg or caterpillar in your garden.
Describe how a caterpillar eats and grows.
Use the new words for the parts of a butterfly.
Watch a butterfly safely and let it go.

sections.body:
A butterfly is an insect with big, bright wings. It drinks sweet flower juice with a long tongue.

Every butterfly starts life as a tiny egg. The egg rests on a leaf, often under it. Then something small and hungry hatches out.

That little creature is a **caterpillar**. It eats leaves and grows very fast. In a few weeks it becomes too big for its old skin.

Then the caterpillar makes a soft case around itself and hides inside. Inside the case, its body changes in an amazing way.

When the case splits open, a butterfly comes out. Its wings are soft and wet at first. It hangs still and lets them dry.

This whole journey has a name. It is called a **life cycle**. The butterfly grows, changes, and one day lays eggs of its own.

Butterflies are not strong flyers when they leave. Their wings must harden in the sun before they can fly well.
examples: A butterfly starts life as a tiny egg on a leaf.
The caterpillar eats leaves and grows very fast.
The butterfly hangs still while its wings dry.
sections.heading: What a butterfly is, and where it begins

sections.body:
Look closely at a butterfly and you cannot see where the caterpillar went. But if you watch from the start, the four stages are easy to spot.

**Stage one: the egg.** The female butterfly lays her eggs on a plant. She chooses the right plant, because that is what the baby will eat. The egg is so small that you may need to look for it with care. Some eggs are green, some white, some golden.

**Stage two: the caterpillar.** The egg hatches into a larva, which is another word for caterpillar. It eats almost all the time. It grows, and then it sheds its skin and grows more. A caterpillar may shed its skin four or five times.

**Stage three: the chrysalis.** When the caterpillar is big enough, it finds a safe place. It makes a case for itself called a **pupa**. For a butterfly, this case is called a chrysalis. It often hangs from a leaf or a twig. Inside, the caterpillar melts into a liquid and builds its new body. This is the strangest part of the whole journey.

**Stage four: the butterfly.** The chrysalis turns clear and thin. The butterfly pushes out and hangs from the empty shell. Its wings fold and hang like wet cloth. After a short rest, it opens them and tests them in the sun.

Then the whole cycle begins again.
examples: The eggs are green and tiny, on the underside of a leaf.
The caterpillar sheds its skin and gets bigger.
The chrysalis hangs from a twig and looks like a little jewel.
sections.heading: The four stages of every butterfly

sections.body:
You do not need a big garden. A balcony with flowers, or a bush near your school, is enough. If you are patient, you can follow one butterfly from egg to flight.

Look for eggs under leaves. Check the plants your butterflies visit. Take a photo so you can find the same spot again.

Keep the plant in a pot with water. Never move a chrysalis from its branch. It is holding on very tightly, and moving it can hurt the butterfly inside.

When the butterfly opens, let it rest. It needs a few quiet minutes to dry its wings. Then you can watch it fly away, and it will come back to your flowers.
examples: I found a green egg under this leaf.
I will check this same branch every morning.
The butterfly is resting, so I wait quietly.
sections.heading: How to watch a butterfly grow
steps: Find eggs on the leaves of the plants that butterflies visit.
Take a photo and write the date next to it.
Keep the plant in water, in a pot or a jar.
Check the same spot every two or three days.
Leave the chrysalis exactly where it hangs.
Let the new butterfly fly away when it is ready.

sections.body:
These are the words you will need when you talk about butterflies.

A **life cycle** is the whole journey of an animal, from egg to adult and back to eggs again.

A **larva** is the young stage. For a butterfly it is the caterpillar. For a frog it is called a tadpole.

A **pupa** is the resting stage. A butterfly's pupa is called a chrysalis. A moth's pupa is called a cocoon.

**Metamorphosis** means a big change of shape. A butterfly changes its whole body as it grows.

**Antennae** are the two thin feelers on a butterfly's head. They help it smell flowers and find a partner.

**Nectar** is the sweet juice inside a flower. Butterflies drink it with a long tube mouth called a proboscis.
sections.heading: The words about butterflies, one by one

terms.example: A butterfly's life cycle has four stages.
terms.gloss: The whole journey of an animal, from the egg all the way back to eggs again.

terms.example: The larva eats and eats until it is fat.
terms.gloss: The young stage of an insect. A butterfly larva is a caterpillar.

terms.example: Inside the pupa, the caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
terms.gloss: The resting stage, when the insect changes its body. A butterfly's pupa is a chrysalis.

terms.example: You can watch metamorphosis happen in a garden.
terms.gloss: A big change of shape. A caterpillar turning into a butterfly is metamorphosis.

terms.example: The butterfly uses its antennae to find the flowers.
terms.gloss: The two thin feelers on an insect's head. They help it smell and feel its way.

sections.body:
A caterpillar has one job, and it does it better than almost any other animal. It eats.

It eats the leaf it is sitting on. It eats so much that you can sometimes hear it chewing. Some caterpillars eat only at night and hide in the morning.

As it eats, the caterpillar grows. Its skin does not stretch, so it becomes too tight. Then the caterpillar does something clever. It splits its old skin and wriggles out of it.

The old skin is often left behind, like a tiny pale shirt on the leaf. Underneath, the caterpillar has a new, bigger skin.

Some caterpillars make silk. It comes out of their mouth as a thin thread. They use it to hang safely, to build a little shelter, or to pull themselves along.

When the caterpillar is fully grown, it stops eating for a while. Then it goes looking for the right place to rest. That is the moment when the chrysalis begins.
examples: The caterpillar is eating the whole leaf.
This is the old skin it grew out of.
The caterpillar is looking for a place to hide.
sections.heading: How a caterpillar eats and grows

sections.body:
Butterflies are delicate. Their wings are thin and their bodies are small. A kind watcher touches less and watches more.

Never pull a chrysalis off its branch. It is glued there with silk, and the butterfly inside may not survive the move.

Do not touch the wings of a butterfly that is resting. A finger on a wet wing can damage it for good.

Keep your hands clean before you handle a caterpillar. Wash your hands afterwards, too, because some caterpillars have prickly hairs.

And if you find a caterpillar on a path, move it gently onto a leaf. Never pick up a butterfly you find lying on the ground. It may just be resting, and it will fly when it is ready.
examples: I will watch it without touching.
I moved the caterpillar onto a leaf.
I washed my hands after touching the caterpillar.
sections.heading: How to be a kind butterfly watcher

item.summary: Butterflies do not arrive in the world as butterflies. They start as eggs and change their whole shape. After reading this, you can name the four stages of a butterfly, tell a caterpillar from a chrysalis, and help a butterfly grow in your garden without hurting it.
item.title: How Butterflies Grow and Change
